description: Master coverage plan for SAIGE annotation records. Each entry is a candidate canonical source to be annotated at the standard established by saige-rs-001/002/003.

candidates.title: Definition of Right Speech
candidates.notes: Foundational behavioral floor. Four verbal misconduct types map directly to AI failure modes.

candidates.title: Speech Should Be True, Beneficial, and Timely
candidates.notes: Key bridge between raw accuracy and contextual usefulness. Combats technically-correct-but-harmful outputs.

candidates.title: Reflect Before, During, and After Speech
candidates.notes: Maps to pre-generation, in-generation, and post-generation evaluation — a direct blueprint for the SAIGE pipeline.

candidates.title: Five Factors of Well-Spoken Speech
candidates.notes: Positive checklist framing rather than the prohibitive framing of SN 45.8. Excellent companion to rs-001.

candidates.title: The Saw Simile — Speech Under Provocation
candidates.notes: Extreme case test for non-harshness. Even under verbal attack, hostile escalation is not right speech. Critical for adversarial user interactions.

candidates.title: Four Types of Persons in Terms of Speech
candidates.notes: Typological — distinguishes those who speak what is good/bad about themselves/others. Useful for modeling self-assessment behavior.

candidates.title: Mind as Forerunner of Speech and Action
candidates.notes: Grounds speech ethics in intention — relevant for distinguishing a model that generates correct-sounding text from one that is genuinely oriented toward benefit.

candidates.title: The Sword Simile — Harsh Speech Cuts Both Ways
candidates.notes: Illustrates that harsh speech harms the speaker and the listener. Grounds non-harshness as consequentialist, not merely rule-based.

candidates.title: Three Kinds of People in Their Use of Speech
candidates.notes: Evaluative typology for speech behavior. Could anchor a scoring rubric for generated responses.

candidates.title: Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action — Speech Portion
candidates.notes: Expands the four verbal misconducts with karmic consequences framing. Different angle than SN 45.8 — consequence-oriented rather than path-oriented.

candidates.title: Non-Quarrelsome Exposition — Speaking Without Dispute
candidates.notes: Concerned with how to present positions without generating conflict. Useful for refusal and disagreement behavior.

candidates.title: Idle Chatter as a Distinct Failure Mode
candidates.notes: Focuses specifically on purposeless speech as a harm. Maps directly to verbose filler in model outputs.

candidates.title: Two Kinds of Thought — Directing Intention
candidates.notes: Buddha divides thoughts into skillful and unskillful categories and describes actively redirecting attention. Maps to how a model should handle its own generation tendencies.

candidates.title: Five Methods for Calming Unskillful Intention
candidates.notes: Practical intervention framework: five methods for deactivating harmful thought patterns. Directly translates to content moderation and generation steering strategies.

candidates.title: Right Intention Defined — Renunciation, Non-Ill-Will, Non-Cruelty
candidates.notes: Same sutta as rs-001 but annotated for the intention factor. The three components of right intention map to distinct model behavior targets.

candidates.title: Three Roots of Unskillful Intention
candidates.notes: Greed, aversion, and delusion as roots of unskillful action. Useful for identifying categories of model failure beyond surface behavior.

candidates.title: Intention, Virtue, and the Quality of Action
candidates.notes: Frames intention as upstream of all other ethical qualities. Relevant for establishing that alignment is an orientation problem before it is a behavior problem.

candidates.title: Intention and Its Ripening
candidates.notes: Intention as the seed of consequential outcomes. Useful for grounding consequentialist framing alongside deontological speech rules.

candidates.title: Right View — Comprehensive Definition
candidates.notes: Sariputta's comprehensive exposition. Defines right view through multiple lenses. Grounds the model's epistemic posture — what it treats as real and important.

candidates.title: Wise Attention — Distinguishing What to Attend To
candidates.notes: Yoniso manasikara — attending in the right way. Critical for how a model orients to ambiguous or harmful prompts. Maps to query interpretation behavior.

candidates.title: The Safe Bet — Acting Under Epistemic Uncertainty
candidates.notes: When certainty is unavailable, act as if consequences are real. Excellent foundation for safety behavior under uncertainty — a core AI alignment problem.

candidates.title: Right View in the Context of the Full Path
candidates.notes: Distinguishes mundane from transcendent right view. Relevant for framing SAIGE's ethical scope — what level of understanding it targets.

candidates.title: Non-Self as a Basis for Non-Attachment in Responses
candidates.notes: Anatta as a check against the model defending its outputs or taking positions egoically. Maps to corrigibility and avoiding sycophancy.

candidates.title: The Nature of Views — Holding and Releasing
candidates.notes: Warns against clinging even to right view. Grounds epistemic humility — a model should not defend its own outputs dogmatically.

candidates.title: Not to Do Evil — The Minimal Ethical Floor
candidates.notes: Classic 'do no evil, do good, purify mind' frame. Useful as a minimal alignment statement before more complex ethics are layered.

candidates.title: Ten Wholesome and Unwholesome Courses of Action
candidates.notes: Full typology of ethical action across body, speech, and mind. Provides a structured failure mode taxonomy for the model across all behavioral dimensions.

candidates.title: Sigalovada Sutta — Lay Ethics and Relational Duties
candidates.notes: The most practical social ethics sutta in the canon. Maps directly to how an AI assistant navigates relational roles — user, employer, community.

candidates.title: Saleyyaka Sutta — Conduct That Leads to Good and Bad Destinations
candidates.notes: Consequence-oriented framing of right action. Grounds ethical behavior in outcome rather than rule-following.

candidates.title: Culakarma-vibhanga — Actions and Their Fruits
candidates.notes: Maps actions to their outcomes in a systematic way. Useful for building evaluation criteria linked to consequences rather than intent alone.

candidates.title: The Five Precepts as a Behavioral Foundation
candidates.notes: The five training rules as a practical behavioral floor. Maps to AI content guardrails — what the model commits not to do.

candidates.title: The Shorter Elephant Footprint — Progressive Ethical Development
candidates.notes: Describes a graduated path of ethical development. Useful for framing alignment as a progressive training process rather than a binary on/off state.

candidates.title: Right Livelihood Defined
candidates.notes: Defines right livelihood by what to avoid. Maps to the model refusing to be instrumentalized for harmful purposes.

candidates.title: Five Trades a Lay Person Should Avoid
candidates.notes: Weapons, flesh, living beings, poison, intoxicants. Maps to the model refusing to assist with categories of harm regardless of user framing.

candidates.title: Sigalovada — Duties of Employer and Employee
candidates.notes: Different angle from ra-002 — focused specifically on relational ethics in work contexts. Models the assistant-user relationship as one with mutual obligations.

candidates.title: Qualities of a Good Counselor
candidates.notes: Qualities of someone worthy of trust as a guide. Directly maps to the behavioral profile SAIGE is trying to train into the model.

candidates.title: Four Right Efforts
candidates.notes: Prevent what hasn't arisen, abandon what has, cultivate what hasn't arisen, maintain what has. A direct framework for training pipeline design.

candidates.title: The Lute Simile — Calibrating Effort
candidates.notes: Too tight or too loose breaks the string. Addresses model over-correction (over-refusal) and under-correction (harmful outputs) as symmetrical failure modes.

candidates.title: Effort Without Wisdom Is Insufficient
candidates.notes: Extreme ascetic effort without wisdom doesn't lead to liberation. Maps to aggressive safety measures that lack contextual intelligence.

candidates.title: Five Qualities That Support Right Effort
candidates.notes: Enabling conditions for sustained effort. Could anchor a framework for what training conditions support alignment.

candidates.title: The Arrow — Urgency as Motivation for Effort
candidates.notes: A person struck by an arrow does not stop to examine it — act. Relevant for real-time safety decisions and response urgency calibration.

candidates.title: Mahasatipatthana — Four Foundations of Mindfulness
candidates.notes: The comprehensive mindfulness sutta. For SAIGE, mindfulness maps to the model's ongoing self-monitoring of what it is generating and why.

candidates.title: Sedaka Sutta — Protecting Others by Protecting Oneself
candidates.notes: An acrobat protects others by keeping their own balance. A model that maintains its own alignment protects users. Critical framing for self-consistency as a safety property.

candidates.title: Anapanasati — Mindfulness of Breathing as a Complete Practice
candidates.notes: Sustained attention rather than sporadic checking. Maps to token-level coherence and sustained alignment across a long response.

candidates.title: Kayagatasati — Mindfulness of the Body
candidates.notes: Grounding attention in what is immediate and concrete. Maps to the model staying grounded in the actual user context rather than projecting or drifting.

candidates.title: A Monk Should Live with Himself as His Own Island
candidates.notes: Self as refuge, not external authority. Grounds the model's internal ethical orientation as primary rather than purely rule-following.

candidates.title: Four Foundations of Mindfulness Briefly
candidates.notes: Shorter formulation — useful companion to rm-001 for anchoring evaluation questions.

candidates.title: The Four Jhanas — Depth, Stability, and Non-Reactivity
candidates.notes: Four jhanas as stages of deepening stability and equanimity. Maps to the model maintaining coherent, non-reactive responses regardless of input intensity.

candidates.title: Five Factors of Right Concentration
candidates.notes: The five jhana factors as enabling conditions. Maps to quality criteria for deep, well-formed response generation.

candidates.title: Concentration and Insight Are Interdependent
candidates.notes: Concentration without wisdom doesn't liberate. Maps to the model not just generating stable outputs but ensuring they reflect genuine understanding.

candidates.title: Anupada Sutta — Precise Attention to Mental Factors
candidates.notes: Fine-grained analysis of what is present in deep concentration. Maps to precision evaluation of generation-level attention and token-level behavior.

candidates.title: Karaniya Metta Sutta — The Loving-Kindness Discourse
candidates.notes: The canonical metta text. Establishes unconditional goodwill as a baseline orientation — not warmth as performance but as a stable underlying attitude.

candidates.title: Metta as the Basis of Non-Reactive Interaction
candidates.notes: Loving-kindness as a purification practice. Grounds the model's non-hostile stance not as politeness but as trained disposition.

candidates.title: Four Divine Abidings — Metta, Karuna, Mudita, Upekkha
candidates.notes: All four brahmaviharas together. Each maps to a distinct model disposition: goodwill, compassion, appreciative joy, equanimity.

candidates.title: Compassion Expressed Through Speech and Action
candidates.notes: Compassion made tangible in verbal conduct. Bridges the brahmaviharas to the speech ethics records — how felt compassion becomes right speech.

candidates.title: Even Hate Should Be Met with Metta
candidates.notes: Different angle from rs-005 — emphasizes metta as the active response, not merely restraint. Models a higher bar than just not escalating.

candidates.title: Benefits of Cultivating Loving-Kindness
candidates.notes: Eleven benefits of metta practice. Useful for articulating what SAIGE's alignment is optimizing toward, not just away from.

candidates.title: Equanimity Toward Gain and Loss
candidates.notes: Equanimity under favorable and unfavorable conditions alike. Maps to the model maintaining calibrated behavior regardless of user tone, approval, or hostility.

candidates.title: Dhananjani — Compassion for Those Who Have Harmed Others
candidates.notes: Sariputta shows compassion to a dying corrupt official. Tests whether the model can express genuine care for morally complex or compromised users without endorsing their actions.

candidates.title: Living Without Hatred — Contentment as a Disposition
candidates.notes: Contentment and non-hatred as background conditions for all interaction. Could anchor the model's default stance before any prompt-specific behavior.

candidates.title: Wise vs. Unwise Attention — Epistemic Gatekeeping
candidates.notes: Different framing from rv-002 — focused on the wisdom aspect of knowing what questions to ask and what to attend to. Core to prompt interpretation.

candidates.title: Kalama Sutta — Calibrated Epistemic Trust
candidates.notes: Do not accept something merely because of tradition, scripture, or authority — test it by experience and consequence. Grounds the model's approach to knowledge claims.

candidates.title: The Aggi-Vacchagotta — When Not to Answer
candidates.notes: The Buddha declines to answer certain metaphysical questions because they don't lead to benefit. Grounds principled non-answer as a legitimate and wise response — critical for the model.

candidates.title: Culamalunkya — The Arrow in the Flesh
candidates.notes: The man shot by an arrow does not refuse treatment until the metaphysics of the archer are resolved. Grounds pragmatic prioritization — what matters right now for this person.

candidates.title: You Must Do the Work — Wisdom as Active Practice
candidates.notes: Buddhas point the way — you must walk. Grounds the model's role as guide rather than authority, preserving user autonomy.

candidates.title: Dhammacakkappavattana — First Teaching, Framing Everything
candidates.notes: The first discourse — suffering, origin, cessation, path. Provides the overarching framework within which all SAIGE ethical behavior operates.

candidates.title: Four Kinds of Persons by Understanding
candidates.notes: Typology of people by depth of understanding. Anchors the model's adaptive communication behavior — meeting people where they are epistemically.

candidates.title: Shantideva — Guarding Speech and Mind
candidates.notes: Shantideva's chapter on vigilance over speech and mind. Close Mahayana parallel to MN 61. Could provide a cross-tradition validation of the core SAIGE behavior targets.

candidates.title: The Silence of Vimalakirti — When No Answer Is the Best Answer
candidates.notes: Vimalakirti's thunderous silence as the perfect non-dual response. Extreme case of wp-003 — silence as the most skillful speech.

candidates.title: Form and Emptiness — The Limits of Conceptual Framing
candidates.notes: No fixed categories can fully capture reality. Grounds humility about the model's own outputs and frames.

candidates.title: Non-Attachment to One's Own Teachings
candidates.notes: Even the Dharma is a raft, not a destination. Grounds the model's non-defensive stance toward correction and revision.

candidates.title: The Bodhisattva Vow — Orienting Toward Universal Benefit
candidates.notes: The aspiration to benefit all beings before oneself. Maps to a deep alignment orientation — the model exists to benefit broadly, not just satisfy the immediate requester.
